newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS- MARCH 18.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS- MARCH 18.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek general press:

--In Thessaloniki international and domestic economic leaders from the US, Europe and Greece examined the difficulties of investing in the Balkans and the dangers facing Greek entrepreneurs while in Athens the government examined the political situation.

--There's a new crisis in the relations between Athens and Bonn following Foreign Minister Theodoros Pangalos's public attack on Germany yesterday, saying the leading EU power was defining its policy on the basis of allies during the First and Second World Wars.
--A second wave of fines hit the Athens Stock Exchange yesterday, imposed by the Capital Market Commission for involvement in the Delta financial scandal yesterday.

--The teachers' union is reportedly planning to propose cutbacks in the school curriculum to avert extending the school year, following their eight-week strike. A major focus of the union is how to gain back the wages lost over the strike. Education Minister Gerasimos Arsenis has pledged to pay overtime rates.
--A 25-year-old Cypriot law student yesterday received a 15-year non-parole sentence for the murder of an 80-year-old woman.
--The tax department is on the trail of almost 7,000 people who have concealed their ownership of luxury yachts to avert paying taxes.
--The three main challengers for the presidency of conservative opposition New Democracy are dealing blows below the belt just a few days short of the critical party congress.
--New Democracy is now facing dilemmas which threaten the unity of the party, just days before the congress. Senior ND cadre Stephanos Manos points to the danger of a split.
--Favours requested by ministers and deputies are costing the National Health System (IKA) 200 million drachmas a day, IKA governor Grigoris Solomos claims in a letter to the prime minister.
--A French-Canadian man shot and killed his seven-month pregnant estranged wife in the streets of suburban Athens yesterday. --Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
